{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-de-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"de2e2e75bd04fa5d62c2de8d7ec076bcbe2b9f0acccd6fae9707606b3df072c1","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-de-class-d:lineage:20","source_registry_sha256":"7b6c7aeec232df29a8679bf39181604be2d91ce9a1cb4fcc709fed49cbe724bb","source_liveness_sha256":"53bd779b9965bd9d51630c8d8d055ccdc52a4d8ec7117a3b87241fc5129eb44f"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"License eligibility, identity and application","heading":"C2 — License eligibility, identity and application","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — License eligibility, identity and application

FACT_ID: sec02-R01 | anchor: A07
A birth certificate presented for an applicant younger than 18 must include the birth parents’ names. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec02-R02 | anchor: A07
An applicant younger than 18 or eligible for the IEP graduated-license program must present a document identifying the parents or legal guardians. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec02-R03 | anchor: A07
A valid foreign passport offered as identity proof also requires the appropriate immigration document. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec02-R04 | anchor: A07
A consular report of birth abroad is listed as acceptable identity and lawful-presence documentation. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec02-R05 | anchor: A07
A certificate of naturalization is listed among acceptable identity and lawful-presence documents. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec02-R06 | anchor: A07
A certificate of citizenship is listed among acceptable identity and lawful-presence documents. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec02-R07 | anchor: A07
A valid U.S. passport is listed among acceptable identity and lawful-presence documents. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec02-R08 | anchor: A07
A permanent-resident re-entry permit is listed among acceptable identity and lawful-presence documents. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec02-R09 | anchor: A07
A refugee travel document is listed among acceptable identity and lawful-presence documents. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec02-R10 | anchor: A07
An employment authorization card is listed among acceptable identity and lawful-presence documents. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec02-R11 | anchor: A08
A court order used under the alternate identity-document list must show the full name, birth date and court seal, requires accompanying citizenship or lawful-presence proof, and is not an acceptable document for federally compliant identification. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec02-R12 | anchor: A08
An abstract of a criminal or civil conviction does not qualify as the court order in the alternate identity-document list. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec02-R13 | anchor: A08
A state photo driver license from the alternate-document list requires accompanying citizenship or lawful-presence proof and does not qualify under that list for federal-compliant identification. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec02-R14 | anchor: A08
A certified school record or transcript used from the alternate-document list must verify full name and birth date, requires citizenship or lawful-presence proof, and does not qualify for federal-compliant identification. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec02-R15 | anchor: A08
A Social Security card is accepted as proof of a Social Security number. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec02-R16 | anchor: A08
A W-2 tax form is accepted as proof of a Social Security number. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec02-R17 | anchor: A08
A pay stub used to prove a Social Security number must display the full number. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec02-R18 | anchor: A08
A Medicare or Medicaid card is not acceptable Social Security-number proof. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec02-R19 | anchor: A08
An SSA ineligibility letter cannot support issuance of federally compliant identification, although a noncompliant document may be available. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec02-R20 | anchor: A08
The two residence proofs must come from different sources and show the person’s physical home address rather than a post-office box. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec02-R21 | anchor: A08
Residence-proof mail must have been delivered by USPS and postmarked or received during the preceding 60 days. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec02-R22 | anchor: A08
Residence-proof mail delivered by UPS, FedEx or DHL is unacceptable. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec02-R23 | anchor: A08
Personal letters and cards from nonbusiness senders cannot serve as residence proof. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec02-R24 | anchor: A08
Utility bills, credit-card statements, bank records, employment records, auto or life insurance policies and rental agreements are listed as residence-proof sources. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec02-R25 | anchor: A09
A person with multiple legal name changes must provide the documents covering every change. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec02-R26 | anchor: A09
An applicant changing a name must update Social Security records and wait 48 hours before visiting the DMV. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec02-R27 | anchor: A09
A valid marriage license or civil-union certificate used for a legal name change must be government-issued and bear a raised seal. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec02-R28 | anchor: A09
A marriage certificate signed by clergy is not acceptable proof for the stated name-change requirement. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec02-R29 | anchor: A09
A finalized divorce decree can authorize return to a previous name only if it identifies both names and permits the return. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec02-R30 | anchor: A09
A minor born outside the United States who was adopted must establish citizenship or lawful presence even when the adoptive parent is a U.S. citizen. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec02-R31 | anchor: A09
For a foreign-born adopted minor presenting a foreign birth certificate with citizenship or lawful-presence proof, mismatched names require evidence of the legal name change. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec02-R32 | anchor: A09
For a foreign-born adopted minor, adoption paperwork is required when the birth certificate does not identify the adoptive parents. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec02-R33 | anchor: A09
Foreign-adoption documents must be originals or certified copies, and a certified English translation may also be required. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec02-R34 | anchor: A09
A Delaware Driving Privilege Card authorizes driving within Delaware and cannot be used as valid identification. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec02-R35 | anchor: A09
A Driving Privilege Card is available only to eligible foreign Delaware residents who cannot document lawful U.S. presence. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec02-R36 | anchor: A09
U.S. citizens and people possessing valid lawful-presence documents cannot obtain a Driving Privilege Card. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec02-R37 | anchor: A09
A Driving Privilege Card costs $20 and remains valid for four years. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec02-R38 | anchor: A10
Driving Privilege Card holders remain subject to Delaware’s driving laws and rules. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec02-R39 | anchor: A10
A Driving Privilege Card applicant begins the process by arranging an appointment with the State Bureau of Identification. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec02-R40 | anchor: A10
The State Bureau of Identification collects the Driving Privilege Card applicant’s fingerprints, validates identity and provides a receipt. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec02-R41 | anchor: A10
A Driving Privilege Card applicant must obtain certification from the Division of Revenue showing Delaware tax filings for the preceding two years. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec02-R42 | anchor: A10
Foreign-language documents presented for a Driving Privilege Card must accompany a professional English translation. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec02-R43 | anchor: A10
The Driving Privilege Card document package includes the SBI receipt, tax-filing certification, name and birth-date proof, applicable name-change proof and two separate Delaware residence proofs. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec02-R44 | anchor: A10
A Driving Privilege Card applicant younger than 18 must also supply the original birth certificate and its translated copy. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec02-R45 | anchor: A10
Driving Privilege Card applicants must sign the application and undergo vision, written and road-skills testing. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec02-R46 | anchor: A11
The DMV verifies the applicant’s State Bureau of Identification receipt with SBI during the Driving Privilege Card application. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec02-R47 | anchor: A11
The DMV verifies the Driving Privilege Card applicant’s tax-filing document with the Division of Revenue. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec02-R48 | anchor: A11
A valid unexpired foreign passport may establish a Driving Privilege Card applicant’s identity if the DMV approves and electronically verifies it. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec02-R49 | anchor: A11
A valid unexpired consular identity document issued by the applicant’s country of citizenship may establish identity if the DMV approves and electronically verifies it. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec02-R50 | anchor: A11
The Mexican Federal Electoral Card is listed as an alternate approved identity document for a Driving Privilege Card applicant from Mexico. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec02-R51 | anchor: A10
Driving Privilege Card applicants must present original or certified documents; photocopied, altered or expired documents are not accepted. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec02-R52 | anchor: A10
The handbook states that the State Bureau of Identification collects a $72 fee while fingerprinting and validating a Driving Privilege Card applicant’s identity. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0025]
